title: Lesson 9: Fighting for Purity
description: Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him. Through King David's fall, Jesus' words about the heart, and 1 Corinthians 6, you will learn what to do when temptation arrives: R-U-N. Remember the Cross, United with God, and Need others. And when we fail, repentance is needed, and forgiveness is given.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, the Closer to God Triangle showed that as two people draw near to God, they draw near to each other. Temptation pulls the opposite way, away from God and away from the people you love. This lesson is about purity, which means guarding your body, your eyes, and your mind, whether you are married or single. Like everything in the Christian life, it starts with grace.

blocks.alt: King David, fully clothed, alone on his palace roof overlooking the city, with his royal robe and crown set aside

blocks.title: The View from the Roof
blocks.text:
David was Israel's greatest king, a man after God's own heart (1 Samuel 13:14). One spring, when kings went out to battle, David stayed home. Late one afternoon he walked on his palace roof and saw a woman bathing. Instead of turning away, he kept looking. He learned she was Bathsheba, the wife of one of his soldiers, and he "sent messengers and took her" (2 Samuel 11:4).

When Bathsheba became pregnant, David tried to cover it up. When that failed, he had her husband, Uriah, killed in battle. One look became a string of choices, and each one made the next one easier. "But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD" (2 Samuel 11:27). David hid his sin and stayed silent, until God sent him someone.

David's story is a warning. Years before, another leader faced a similar temptation in the house of Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, and chose to flee. When he was tempted, Joseph "left his garment in her hand and fled" (Genesis 39:12). Joseph ran from sin, and David did not. Sin comes to steal, kill, and destroy, but Jesus came to give life.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.
9.1 - Consider David's story: a look, then a sinful action, and then the hiding and the cover-up. Why do you think that first step matters so much when responding to temptation?
R-U-N from Sin
Paul wrote to young Christians in Corinth, a city full of sexual temptation. He told them to RUN.

But he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him. Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

Flee means run. When temptation arrives, you have a split second to choose: run toward life, or stay and slide toward the pit. Do not see how close you can get. Close the app, turn off the show, or leave the room. Try it below.

R is for Remember the Cross. Temptation says your body is yours to use however you want. Paul says you are not your own, because you were bought with a price. Count the cost. Your forgiveness was bought with the life of God's own Son. Dietrich Bonhoeffer put it this way: "what has cost God much cannot be cheap for us." Grace is free, but it is never cheap. It never whispers, "Go ahead, you will be forgiven anyway."
What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?

You are forgiven, fully and freely. But grace does not just cancel your debt. It makes you new, so you do not keep on sinning. You are not fighting for purity so God will let you into His family. You are fighting because you are already in it, loved by a Father who paid everything to set you free.
9.2 - How can remembering that Jesus died on the cross for your forgiveness help you fight temptation?
U is for United with God. You are joined to the Lord, Christ is in you, and your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19).
N is for Need others. Sin grows best in hiding, just as it did for David. Notice all the 2s in 2 Timothy 2:22, and let them remind you to run with another.
So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

The 2s do not mean you need two more people. They mean you need another, so there are two of you. Nathan was David's other. God sent the prophet to the king, and Nathan told him a story about a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb. David burned with anger, and Nathan said, "You are the man!" (2 Samuel 12:7). Nathan shows what a good "other" does:

He comes close. Nathan went to David instead of talking about him. He tells the truth. Nathan loved David too much to let him keep hiding. He points to grace. When David said, "I have sinned against the LORD," Nathan answered, "The LORD also has put away your sin" (2 Samuel 12:13). Ask God for your Nathan, and be ready to be one for someone else.
When the Thought Knocks
Purity starts in the heart. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said:
You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.' But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

A passing thought is not a sin, since Jesus Himself was tempted. A tempting thought is a knock at the door. Lust is opening the door and letting it stay (James 1:14-15). Job decided ahead of time what he would do with his eyes:
I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a young woman.

So when the thought knocks, run. Paul says to "take every thought captive to obey Christ" (2 Corinthians 10:5). Name the thought, hand it to Jesus, and choose what is good. Do not believe the lies temptation tells, like "No one will know" or "You're too far gone." Jesus called the devil a liar (John 8:44). Answer with the truth: Christ bought you at the cross, God lives in you, and you are not alone.
9.3 - What is one habit or boundary you can establish to better protect your mind and heart?
When You Fall, Repent
Maybe you read David's story and thought, "That is me." Look at what David did when Nathan confronted him. He did not make excuses. He repented, and later he wrote:
I acknowledged my sin to you, and I did not cover my iniquity; I said, "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD," and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.

Repentance is not just feeling bad. It is three simple steps back to God. Confess it. Stop hiding and agree with God about your sin by name. Turn from it. Walk away from the sin and back toward God, and take the RUN plan with you. Receive forgiveness. "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins" (1 John 1:9), and "there is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1). Growth can be slow, but God has not given up on you.

blocks.title: If you have been hurt
content: If someone has hurt you, please do not carry it alone. Seek help from someone safe, like a healthy family member, a pastor, or a teacher.

blocks.text: 9.4 - Who is one mature, trusted believer you could ask to pray for you and check in with you about purity? What would help you take that step? You do not need to write any private details here.
Lesson 9 Review

David did not run. His fall began with a look and grew in hiding, until God sent Nathan with the truth and David repented (Psalm 32:5). Grace is free, but it is never cheap, because it cost God His Son. Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him and the relationships inside the Closer to God Triangle. When temptation arrives, R-U-N: Remember the Cross, United with God, and Need others. And when you fall, repent and receive His forgiveness. In the next lesson, you will come to the table Jesus set for His people, where that same costly grace is put on display.
